messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] PD: pd-ml-inference (P2) — spike in inference service error-rate on region-east. root alert ts=3023456789, metric=inference_5xx_rate > 1.5%
jen_sre: seeing it on the latency/error dashboard. a few hosts are reporting KV cache thrash + OOM-ish logs. digging into pods now.
mike_oncall: any clear customer-facing impact? are we hitting retries / client errors?
tara_pm: product reports ~2.2% of search requests are failing with 502s for a subset of users in EU region — not a full outage but visible on SLO. customers flagged one support ticket.
eli_platform: looks correlated with a config push to model-runner yesterday that increased worker count + disabled aggressive prefix caching. rolling back that change might help.
jen_sre: agree. temp mitigation idea: mute noisy alert route and add a brief debounce so oncall can focus on root cause. do we want a PD route-level mute for 20m while we rollback?
mike_oncall: yes please — +1 for short mute. also add an automatic dedupe so repeated host-level triggers don't fan out.
jen_sre: doing a quick runbook step:
```
# quick PD mute (org tooling)
/pd-silence --route pd-ml-inference --duration 20m --reason "KV cache thrash; investigating"
```
jen_sre: executing now. will also add temporary alert throttle: group by "cause:kv-cache" label and set min_interval=300s. that will stop host churn from creating >1 page per host.
pagerduty: Service pd-ml-inference: Silence started by jen_sre for 20 minutes.
eli_platform: started rollback of yesterday's model-runner config in canary (2 nodes). monitoring error rate on canary.
tara_pm: ping when canary stabilizes; we may need to push to prod rollback if errors drop.
jen_sre: observed immediate drop in new unique host alerts after route mute + throttle, but error-rate still elevated on older hosts. can we add prefix/KV cache warmup on restart?
eli_platform: yes, we can enable graceful cache-warm on restart; I'll flip the flag in canary and watch.
mike_oncall: also please add a temporary dashboard tile showing "unique alerting hosts / 5m" so we can see fanout.
jen_sre: done — created panel and pinned to incident channel. URL: https://redwood-internal/dash/alerts?panel=unique_hosts
jen_sre: quick config tweak proposal for follow-up (to avoid repeat noise):
```
- alert: inference_5xx_spike
  expr: increase(inference_5xx[5m]) / increase(requests_total[5m]) > 0.01
  labels:
    severity: high
  for: 2m
  annotations:
    runbook: /runbooks/inference/5xx-spike
  dedupe: group_by=[service,region,root_cause]
  min_interval: 300s
```
jen_sre: action items: 1) eli: finish canary rollback & enable cache-warm (in progress) 2) jen: keep PD route muted for 20m and monitor dedupe throttles 3) mike: follow up with support on the customer ticket and note degraded SLO 4) infra: in 24h, run an experiment that groups alerts by root_cause label and measures oncall pages reduction.
tara_pm: good plan. please capture the post-incident tuning PR with before/after alert counts so we can justify change.
eli_platform: canary looks good — error-rate down ~1.1% on canary after cache-warm. rolling full rollback now.
jen_sre: rolling back complete. watching global error-rate. PD mute expires in ~8m; will re-evaluate before unmute.
mike_oncall: thanks all. from incident POV this was medium-impact but noise amplification was the real burden. the short route mute + dedupe stopped PD storm and let us fix root cause.
jen_sre: closing notes: will open a short PR to add min_interval=300s and group_by root_cause; will also add dashboard panel to alerting team. cc @eng-sre for review.
pagerduty: Silence ended for pd-ml-inference.
jen_sre: unmuted PD route; no new pages in the past 10m. marking this thread resolved.
---
summary: short PD route mute + temporary alert throttle reduced alert storm. root cause: config change that disabled cache warm; rollback + cache-warm fixed customer-facing errors. follow-ups: alert grouping/dedupe + dashboard + post-incident tuning PR.
